name: 80/20 Running (Fitzgerald)

citations.title: 80/20 Running: Run Stronger and Race Faster by Training Slower

description: Polarized training applied to road runners: 80% of weekly running volume at low intensity (Z1-Z2), 20% at moderate-to-high intensity (Z3-Z5). Built on Stephen Seiler's research findings made accessible for amateurs. Explicit 5-zone heart-rate or pace system with plans for 5K through marathon.
signature: 80% easy / 20% moderate-to-hard volume distribution across a 5-zone HR system
philosophyNarrative: Fitzgerald's 80/20 system translates Stephen Seiler's polarized-training research into practical plans for amateur runners. The core insight: most amateur runners run too hard on easy days and too easy on hard days — the dreaded 'gray zone' that produces neither aerobic adaptation nor high-intensity adaptation. Fix this by going EXPLICITLY easy 80% of the time and EXPLICITLY hard 20% of the time. The 5-zone system gives you precise targets: Z1 (recovery), Z2 (aerobic / GA), Z3 (moderate / threshold), Z4 (lactate threshold), Z5 (VO2max). The 80/20 ratio is measured by TIME (not workouts) — so a single hard interval session might count as moderate weekly volume despite hard effort. The system periodizes through Base → Build → Peak → Taper with explicit weekly hard/easy ratios at each phase.

paceZones.purpose: Slowest aerobic running. Heart rate <81% of LTHR. Used for active recovery and the easiest portions of warmup/cooldown.
Aerobic base development. The bulk of weekly mileage in 80/20. HR 81-89% LTHR. Conversational throughout.
Moderate aerobic — the 'gray zone' Fitzgerald warns against for easy days but uses deliberately for marathon-pace work. HR 90-95% LTHR.
Threshold pace, ~96-102% LTHR. Used in tempo runs and threshold intervals. Comfortably hard but not race effort.
Hardest training intensity. >102% LTHR. Used in short intervals (3-5 min reps) at 5K-3K race pace.

rpeRange.description: Hard; cannot speak more than a word

workouts.name: Z2 Easy Run
workouts.shortDescription: Aerobic run held strictly in Zone 2 — the workout that drives 80/20 distribution

mainSet.cue: Strictly Z2 — if HR drifts above 89% LTHR, slow down. The discipline of staying easy IS the workout.

workouts.purpose: The cornerstone workout of 80/20. By holding strictly Z2, you accumulate aerobic adaptation without hidden moderate-intensity creep. This is what the 80% is.
cues: If HR drifts above Z2, slow down — even if it feels too easy
Pace will rise as fitness improves at the same HR
Conversational pace throughout

workouts.name: Z1 Recovery Run
workouts.shortDescription: Very easy short run held in Zone 1 — true recovery effort

mainSet.cue: HR strictly below 81% LTHR. Walking is permitted if HR drifts up.

workouts.purpose: True recovery. Even gentler than Z2. Used between hard sessions to enable adaptation.
cues: Slower than your normal easy pace
Walk breaks fine if HR creeps up
Should feel restorative, not draining

workouts.name: Long Run (Z2)
workouts.shortDescription: Long run held in Zone 2, with optional Z3 segments late in training

mainSet.cue: Hold Z2 even as fatigue accumulates and HR drift wants to push you into Z3. Discipline matters most in the final hour.

workouts.purpose: Endurance building at strict Z2. Late in training, can include 20-30 min in Z3 for marathon specificity.
cues: Watch HR drift — pace must drop to keep HR in Z2
Practice race-day fueling on runs over 90 min
Time on feet matters more than pace

workouts.name: Z3 Progression Run
workouts.shortDescription: Aerobic run building from Z2 to Z3 in the final third — moderate-intensity work

mainSet.cue: Build into Z3. HR should be in the 90-95% LTHR range.

workouts.purpose: Bridges aerobic Z2 work with marathon-pace specificity. Used in late Build phase for marathon and HM runners.
cues: Build gradually into Z3 — don't jump straight to MP
If HR exceeds Z3 (>95% LTHR), slow down
Counts toward the 20% hard portion of weekly volume

workouts.name: Z4 Threshold Tempo
workouts.shortDescription: Continuous tempo run at lactate threshold (Z4)

mainSet.cue: Hold Z4 (96-102% LTHR). About 1-hour race pace. Steady throughout.

workouts.purpose: Lactate threshold development. 80/20 plans use this 1-2× per week in Build and Peak phases.
cues: Tempo pace, not race pace — controlled
If HR drifts above Z4, ease off
Even effort across the duration

workouts.name: Z5 VO2max Intervals
workouts.shortDescription: 3-5 min reps at Zone 5 (>102% LTHR) with equal jog recovery

mainSet.cue: Z5 effort — about 3K-5K race pace. Even pacing across all reps.

workouts.purpose: VO2max development. Used 1× per week in Peak phase. Limited volume — Fitzgerald caps Z5 at 5-8% of weekly volume.
cues: Z5 cap: keep total interval time small relative to weekly volume
First rep at the same effort as the last
End workout if reps slow significantly

workouts.name: Strides
workouts.shortDescription: 8× ~20-sec strides at Z5 effort with full standing recovery

mainSet.cue: Smooth and quick — not maximum sprint.

workouts.purpose: Neuromuscular maintenance during high-volume Z2 work. Tagged onto end of Z2 runs 1-2× per week.
cues: Quick turnover, relaxed shoulders
Skip if very fatigued

phases.name: Base
phases.focus: Establish 80/20 distribution. Build aerobic base in Z2. Strides only as quality.
phases.athleteNarrative: Welcome to 80/20. The first phase establishes the easy/hard distribution. Almost all running is in Zone 2 (HR 81-89% LTHR). Strides are the only quality. The discipline of staying STRICTLY easy on easy days is the foundational skill — many runners will need to slow their easy pace 30-60 sec/mile to hit Z2. Trust this. As fitness improves, your Z2 pace will get faster at the same HR.

phases.name: Build
phases.focus: Add Z4 threshold work and Z3 progression runs. Maintain 80/20 ratio.
phases.athleteNarrative: Build phase. Zone 4 threshold tempos enter (20 min continuous), and Zone 3 progression runs add marathon-specific work for the longer-race plans. Total time in Z3-Z5 stays at ~20% of weekly volume — measured by TIME, not number of workouts. Even with hard work added, the bulk of running is still strict Z2.

phases.name: Peak
phases.focus: Add Z5 VO2max intervals. Peak Z4 tempo volume. Long runs at peak.
phases.athleteNarrative: Peak phase. Z5 VO2max intervals enter the rotation. Z4 tempo volume peaks. Long runs are at maximum. The 80/20 ratio holds — even with two hard sessions per week, the time-volume math still puts you at 80% easy. Recovery between hard sessions is critical.

phases.name: Taper
phases.focus: Reduce Z2 volume sharply; preserve some Z4-Z5 intensity for sharpness.
phases.athleteNarrative: Taper. Volume drops, but intensity is preserved (short Z4 efforts and strides) so you don't go flat. The work is done. Sleep, hydrate, trust the program.

weeklyPatterns.notes: Base 5-day. All Z2 except strides on day 3. Builds the 'discipline of easy' that 80/20 requires.
Build 5-day. Two hard sessions (Tue Z4, Thu Z3) plus Sunday long run. 80/20 time ratio maintained.
Peak 5-day. Z5 intervals + Z4 threshold + long run. 48hr between hard sessions enforced.
Build 6-day. Adds short Monday recovery to increase weekly volume while maintaining 80/20 distribution.
Recovery week. Single quality session, reduced overall volume.

schedule.notes: Z5 intervals — the peak-phase quality anchor

weeklyPatterns.notes: 6-day peak — two quality sessions held inside the 80/20 intensity balance; higher-level plans run six sessions, not five.

taper.notes: Standard 3-week 80/20 taper: 75% / 55% / 40%. Z4 effort preserved early in week 1 to keep intensity sharp.

strengthRecommendation.philosophy: Fitzgerald supports 1-2× weekly strength, focused on running-specific work and core stability. 20-30 min sessions. Schedule on easy days, never adjacent to hard sessions.

crossTrainingRecommendation.intensityGuidance: Cross-training is supplemental. Use only on rest days at Z1-Z2 effort. Counts as 'easy' time toward 80/20 distribution.

restrictions.rule: Requires HR monitor or ability to self-regulate by RPE precisely. The 80/20 ratio depends on accurate intensity measurement.
restrictions.warningMessage: 80/20 works best with a heart-rate monitor and known LTHR. Without HR data, you'll need to self-regulate by RPE/breath — possible but less precise.

restrictions.rule: Beginners often run too hard on easy days; the 80/20 system is harder to apply for runners without baseline aerobic fitness.
restrictions.warningMessage: 80/20 requires the discipline to run very easy. For first-time runners, Higdon Novice is gentler and doesn't require HR-zone discipline.

invariants: Total time at moderate-to-hard (Z3-Z5) must be ≤ 20% of weekly volume
Total time at easy (Z1-Z2) must be ≥ 80% of weekly volume
Z2 must be STRICT — slow down if HR drifts above 89% LTHR even if pace feels too easy
Long run capped at 30% of weekly mileage
Minimum 2 days between any two hard sessions
If user lacks HR monitor or LTHR data, fall back to RPE-based zone targeting
